readme.title: Scores and practice files
readme.poc: Documentation of an agentic AI music workflow and skill as a private code experiment, developed for and with Claude Code. This is a proof of concept only. Use at your own risk.
readme.intro: This package contains the choir parts as scores with lyrics and practice files (audio). It is based on the supplied source {source}.
f_scores: Score (AI version and the supplied scan), MusicXML with choir and piano playback, MIDI files of all voices and the tutti
View, continue editing in a notation program, reuse the MIDI files
f_practice: Overview of the practice files, guide for the director (numbers, abbreviations, hints) and one ZIP per voice "<abbr>_Practice_<title>.zip" with guide, score and the practice MP3s in choir and piano sound; file 6 (tutti) is in every voice ZIP
Entry point for the person who distributes the package; pass the voice ZIPs on as they are
f_tools: Project data (score.json, docs.json, mixes.json, layout.json) and the skill to rebuild
f_docs: README (bilingual), check log, correction log, session handoff (English)
s_accomp: own voice, melody {mel} dB, piano accompaniment {acc} dB
s_choir: neighbours left/right {near} dB, next-but-one {second} dB, others {far} dB
holding one's own in the choir
sound_items: Every audio file exists twice: choir sound and optimised piano (legato).
Soundfont {soundfont}, rendered with FluidSynth, light room reverb, loudness {lufs} LUFS.
The own voice is always centred; the MIDI files carry the same volume and pan values.

Solo and With accompaniment (no. 1 to 4) also exist slowly ({slow_pct} % tempo, "{slow}" in the file name). Before the music the voice's own starting note sounds, then a short pause; file 6 (tutti) starts with the starting notes of all voices one after another (bottom to top). There is a short pause between the verses.
readme.ai_text: The notes were transcribed from the source (scan) with AI assistance, corrected twice against the source and engraved with Verovio (verovio.org). The corrections are listed in the correction log. The sound is software synthesis with a soundfont, not generative AI. The practice files are purely mechanical and exact to the notes; they do not replace an interpretation. The source, decisions and approvals come from people. No guarantee: when in doubt, the source applies.

readme_more.per_voice: Each voice ZIP in {practice} is complete on its own. Only guide, score and file 6 (tutti) exist several times, so that one voice ZIP can be passed on alone. All files and folders start with a number; only the voice ZIPs (and the MIDI folders per voice) start with the abbreviation, for example T1_<title>. All MP3s carry title, album, track and artist tags.

what.choir: The whole choir, your voice a little louder.
what.tutti: The whole choir, all voices equally loud.

guide.intro: Practise with headphones if you can.
tips: Every recording starts with your first note, then a short pause, then the music. Only the last file (all voices equal) starts with the first notes of all voices, one after another.
The number at the start of each file name is the order to practise in.
The two audio folders ("{choir_dir}" and "{piano_dir}" in the name) hold the same recordings, once in choir sound and once in piano sound.
